events.content: Create a single-file HTML page (index.html) with all CSS and JavaScript inline and zero external assets. Render a dark, atmospheric hero scene featuring a single, steaming bowl of vegan ramen as the sole visual focus. Make the dish feel alive and appetizing — with natural motion, ambient warmth, and interactive response to the mouse. Keep the scene pure (no UI, text, or menus), responsive on all screens, and respectful of prefers-reduced-motion.

I’ll build this as a self-contained canvas scene: procedural bowl, broth and toppings, layered steam, warm bloom, and subtle pointer-driven depth. I’ll first inspect the workspace, then implement and run a lightweight browser/syntax check if the project has one.

The workspace is empty, so I’m creating the page from scratch. The composition will stay intentionally restrained: the only defined object is the ramen bowl; depth comes from light, shadow, steam, and the broth itself rather than decorative scenery.

input.command: /bin/zsh -lc "wc -l index.html && sed -n '1,28p' index.html && command -v chromium-browser || command -v chromium || command -v google-chrome || command -v firefox || true && command -v node || true"

events.content: The first pass is in place. I’m rendering it headlessly at desktop and phone dimensions now; that will catch both JavaScript/runtime mistakes and composition issues that a source-only check would miss.

The desktop and phone renders are clean and keep the bowl dominant. I did spot one implementation-level issue during review: the initial paint could start two animation loops, and subsequent resizes could add more. I’m tightening that lifecycle now so the atmosphere stays smooth without unnecessary battery/CPU use.

Created [index.html](<WORKSPACE>/openai/gpt-5.6-sol/xhigh/index.html).

It includes:

- Fully procedural canvas artwork with no external assets
- Animated steam, broth shimmer, warmth, and subtle bowl movement
- Mouse-responsive lighting and parallax
- Responsive desktop/mobile composition
- Static, motion-safe rendering under `prefers-reduced-motion`
- Valid JavaScript and zero external references

Verified through headless Chromium at desktop and phone dimensions.
